profile: node embedding: A node embedding is an associated vector representation for each node, often denoted h_k or stored as columns of node data X. It is a latent/hidden representation, also called an encoding or transformation, learned by a graph neural network. Embeddings can be linearly transformed and combined across the graph for graph-level prediction. An example is a five-dimensional vector attached to a node.

draft.profile: node embedding: A node embedding is an associated vector representation for each node, often denoted h_k or stored as columns of node data X. It is a latent/hidden representation, also called an encoding or transformation, learned by a graph neural network. Embeddings can be linearly transformed in GCN layers and combined across the graph for graph-level prediction. They are designed to be permutation invariant, so the representation does not depend on node indexing. An example is a five-dimensional vector attached to a node.
